tool.name: qiime2 sidle align-regional-kmers
tool.description: Aligns ASV representative sequences to a regional kmer database.
tool.command: export XDG_CONFIG_HOME="\$PWD/xdgconfig" MPLCONFIGDIR="\$PWD/mplconfigdir" NUMBA_CACHE_DIR="\$PWD/numbacache" CONDA_PREFIX=/opt/conda/envs/sidle-0.1.0-beta && q2galaxy run sidle align_regional_kmers '$inputs'

param.name: kmers
param.label: Reference regional kmers
param.help: [required] The reference kmer sequences from the database which have had degenerate sequences expanded and duplicate sequences identified.

param.name: rep_seq
param.label: Representative ASV sequences
param.help: [required] The representative sequences for the ASVs being aligned. These must be a consistent length.

param.name: region
param.label: Region identifier
param.help: [required] A unique description of the hypervariable region being aligned. Ideally, this matches the unique identifier used during the regional extraction.
param.validator: value is not None and len(value) > 0

param.name: max_mismatch
param.label: Maximum nucleotide mismatches
param.help: [default: 2] The maximum number of mismatched nucleotides allowed in mapping between a sequence and kmer.

param.name: chunk_size
param.label: Sequences per processing block
param.help: [default: 100] The number of sequences to be analyzed in parallel blocks. It is highly recommended this number stay relatively small (<1000) in combination with parallel processing (`n_workers`>1) for the best performance and memory optimization.

param.name: debug
param.label: Run without a parallel client
param.help: [default: No] Whether the function should be run in debug mode (without a client) or not. `debug` superceeds all options.

param.name: n_workers
param.label: Parallel workers
param.help: [default: 1] The number of jobs to initiate.

tool.help:
QIIME 2: sidle align-regional-kmers =================================== Aligns ASV representative sequences to a regional kmer database.
Outputs: -------- :regional_alignment.qza: A mapping between the database kmer name and the ASV.
|
Description: ------------ This takes an "amplified" region of the database and performs alignment with representative ASV sequences. The alignment assumes the ASVs and kmers start at the same position in the sequence and that they are the same length.
|
